hotspots.name: Broomhill Road
hotspots.why: Leave and return corridor for the Premier Business Park centre — first and last minutes are marked.
hotspots.speedContext: Treat the exit as a real junction: stop, scan, then commit.

hotspots.name: Greenhills Road
hotspots.why: Busy R819 commuter corridor with chains of light-controlled junctions.
faults: Missing mirrors before pulls and turns
hotspots.speedContext: Steady near-limit progress; scan signs — width does not mean 60.

hotspots.name: Castletymon Road
hotspots.why: Links estates to main roads; estate exits and progress both tested.
faults: Unsafe or timid gap selection onto the main road
hotspots.speedContext: Drop speed into estates; commit safely onto distributors.

hotspots.name: Belgard Road / hospital roundabout area
hotspots.why: Multi-lane roundabout and junction pressure near major flows.
hotspots.speedContext: Early lane position, correct signal, decisive entry when the gap is real.

hotspots.name: Parkhill / Killinarden / Redwood estates
hotspots.why: Tight residential manoeuvre zones with parked cars and gradients.
hotspots.speedContext: Slow, controlled estate speed — observation over progress.

hotspots.name: Tymon / Bancroft
hotspots.why: Restricted-visibility estate exits and manoeuvre practice streets.
hotspots.speedContext: Full stop when required; peep, then move.

tips: Treat leaving Premier Business Park / Broomhill Road as the first marked junction.
Practise Greenhills Road lights in real daytime traffic until lane choice feels automatic.
At Belgard and hospital-area roundabouts, pick your lane early and hold it.
On Parkhill reverse: expect slope plus tight space — control first, then observation.
Tallaght hill starts are steeper than many Dublin centres — zero rollback.
Estate exits in Tymon, Bancroft and Redwood need visible head checks every time.
Do not trust road width for speed — watch 50 → 60 transitions near distributors.
Hesitation on Greenhills and Castletymon is marked as hard as unsafe gaps — be decisive and safe.
Repeat Glenview and Mountain Park turnabouts until mirror checks between moves are automatic.
Use MyRoadSafety cancellations if you want an earlier Tallaght slot.

faqs.q: Where do testers take you on Tallaght driving test routes?
faqs.a: Examiners reuse corridors around Broomhill Road, Greenhills Road, Castletymon Road, Belgard Road, St Aongus, Tymon, Bancroft, Redwood / Treepark, Parkhill and Killinarden — typically within a few kilometres of Premier Business Park.

faqs.q: Where is the reverse around the corner done on the Tallaght test?
faqs.a: Common reverse areas include Killinarden → The Meadows West → Alpine Rise, Redwood Way → Treepark Road → Redwood Walk, Parkhill Road → Parkhill Avenue, and St Aongus Green. Parkhill is especially tight because of slope plus limited space.

faqs.q: Where is the hill start on the Tallaght driving test?
faqs.a: Hill starts often appear on Treepark Road outside Tamarisk Heights, Elmcastle Park beside the field, and Tymonville Park. Gradients here are steeper than many Dublin centres — any rollback is marked.

faqs.q: Where is the turnabout done on the Tallaght test route?
faqs.a: Turnabouts are often done in Glenview Park, from The Heath toward The Oaks / The Meadows East, Avonbeg Park → Mountain Park, and Homelawn Villas toward Mountain Park.

faqs.q: How long is the driving test in Tallaght?
faqs.a: Plan for about 30–40 minutes including checks and manoeuvres, with a drive of at least 7.5 km. Signs, questions and technical checks add time at the centre.

faqs.q: What manoeuvres are on the Tallaght RSA driving test?
faqs.a: Expect reverse around a corner, hill start and turnabout. Parallel parking and bay parking are not the standard RSA car-test manoeuvres used at this centre.

faqs.q: What is the Tallaght driving test pass rate?
faqs.a: The Category B pass rate at Tallaght was 48.5% in July 2026. Source: CSO / RSA driving test statistics (ROA), Category B, July 2026.

faqs.q: How long is the waiting time for a Tallaght driving test?
faqs.a: CSO reported 21 weeks to driving test invite at month end (July 2026). Confirm live slots on MyRoadSafety. Source: CSO / RSA driving test statistics (ROA), Category B, July 2026.

faqs.q: Where is the Tallaght driving test centre?
faqs.a: Premier Business Park, 52 Broomhill Rd, Tallaght, Dublin, D24 VE8E. Always confirm the address on your RSA booking letter.

faqs.q: Can I change my Tallaght driving test date?
faqs.a: If your test is more than 10 days away you can usually change date or time free via MyRoadSafety. Closer than that, cancelling typically means losing the fee unless RSA rules for your situation allow otherwise — check rsa.ie.
